title: messenger-capabilities v1
description: What one messenger says it can do, as data: messengers/<name>/capabilities.json (remote plan step R21, slice 3). A messenger hands one message to one session on its own machine and says how far it got; it knows nothing of links, verbs or other machines. Each capability is declared in the one vocabulary the host and transport capability files use - yes, no, declined or unverified - with its evidence; unverified counts as no, and a capability is yes only with evidence that was run. declined means the messenger chooses not to offer it: the in-process test messenger declares receipt.receiver declined so that no production path can pick it. The list is closed: a messenger declares every one, and nothing else.

body.untyped.description: The body never passes through an input box: it is stored and handed to the session by the session's own side, so no paste can sit unsent, no shell can cut it at a newline and nothing can splice into what someone is typing (wezfleet lib/Mail.ps1, its header).

idempotent.post.description: A second post of one messageId delivers nothing more and returns the stage recorded for the first, so a resend after a dropped link never delivers twice.

receipt.receiver.description: Stage seen is the receiving session's own word: its hook found the message's id in its own transcript. Not the sender's inference from a screen.

wake.description: A target that has ended its turn is woken without its body being typed: at most a one-line notice carrying the id.

evidence.description: What was run or read, and when. Never blank.
